findings.problem: "X plus one goes into four X plus two four times" gives the quotient without saying where the 4 comes from, so a student new to long division won't know how it was found.
findings.fix: Say "four X divided by X is four" before "four times", lighting the 4x and the x as they are named.

findings.problem: "B is negative two" is said, but only the 4 is lit in the line; the −2 on top of the fraction is never pointed out as b.
findings.fix: Wrap the −2 in the d2 tex as its own piece and light it on "B is negative two", in a second colour.

findings.problem: "The sign of the fraction decides it" does not say why the sign matters, so the next three inequality lines arrive without a purpose.
findings.fix: Say "Y is four plus this fraction part, so whether Y is above or below four depends on the sign of the fraction", and light the fraction part of the y = 4 − 2/(x+1) line on those words.

findings.problem: "So every line below four intersects it" rests only on the curve going down forever, which explains low lines but not lines just under four.
findings.fix: Join the two ends in the voice: "it goes down forever near X equals negative one, and comes up close to four as X grows, so it reaches every height below four."

findings.problem: The y = c line is drawn exactly on the dashed asymptote, so its label "c = 4" may sit on top of the "y = 4" label and be unreadable on a phone.
findings.fix: Check the phone frame and move the "c = 4" label to the other end of the line, or above it, so the two labels do not overlap.
